capabilities: Queue papers from Zotero into a staged Triage/Reading/Claim/Assessment workflow
Create paper notes with synced Zotero annotations and placeholder prompts
Record reading decisions, reasons and deferral dates in note properties
Insert quoted annotations with page citations and [[citekey]] links
Export dropped and deferred papers with reasons as a markdown table
extras: Free, with optional Liberapay donations. Runs entirely offline and never connects to the internet. Requires Obsidian 1.13 or later on desktop. Code lives on Codeberg with a copy on GitHub; releases include signed build attestations.
motivation: The author built it because triage decisions made while skimming abstracts were otherwise forgotten, forcing re-reading abstracts a year later and reconstructing literature-selection rationale from memory.
problem: Reference managers help collect papers and annotation tools help read them, but neither tracks the choosing decisions (drop, defer, promote), so those live only in the reader's head.

relations.evidence: It only talks to Zotero, on your own computer.
Paper Trail doesn't run pandoc itself. Exporting is what Due Credit does.
Tag Along shows your vault as a folder tree built from your tags.

summary: Reading-queue plugin that works through a Zotero library in staged passes and records what you decided about each paper.
